applicable_when: The kernel uses 255 registers/thread — the PTX maximum — which hard-limits the SM to only 2 active blocks (8 warps total, 12.5% occupancy). With only 1.96 active warps/scheduler and 58.4% no-eligible cycles, the GPU cannot hide latency. The root cause is the fixed BLOCK_M=128 x BLOCK_N=128 tile with ALLOW_TF32=False forcing full FP32 accumulation across a 128x128 accumulator, consuming all available registers. Reducing tile sizes (e.g., BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64 or BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128) will cut register usage dramatically, allowing 4-8x more warps per SM and enabling latency hiding. Additionally, increasing BLOCK_K from 32 to 64 with num_stages=3 enables software pipelining to overlap memory loads with compute. A @triton.autotune decorator will explore the optimal configuration automatically on the H200.
